concept_title: Counterfactual Co-op: A Time-Machine for First-Years
one_line_thesis: Show first-years their own probable sophomore year twice — brand-only vs balanced — using anonymized NUworks alumni trajectories, delivered as a Power BI story in Teams.

primary_persona.name: Sam Chen
primary_persona.context: Six weeks into fall semester. Has submitted 12 applications — all to Google, Tesla, SpaceX, Apple, and Goldman. Zero applications to SMEs. Spends evenings refreshing application portals and lurking in r/cscareerquestions. Has never heard of any of the 340 SMEs hiring through NUworks this cycle.
primary_persona.emotional_state: Outwardly confident, privately anxious. Believes anything below a FAANG offer would embarrass his family. Hasn't told his advisor he's been ghosted 4x already.

secondary_actors.involvement: Defines what counts as a 'successful sophomore outcome' in the forecast model; reviews anonymization thresholds before launch.
Receives shared forecasts from students; uses them as the opening artifact in 1:1 meetings instead of a blank-page conversation.
Owns the NUworks → Power BI dataflow; enforces k-anonymity (k≥15) before any cohort is rendered.
Approves the anonymization disclosure copy and audits the dataflow quarterly.

demonstrated_moment: Sam opens a Teams notification titled 'Two versions of your sophomore year, Sam.' He taps in. A cinematic split-screen Power BI story renders: 200 anonymized alumni who started his exact major, GPA band, and first-week application pattern — half went brand-only, half went balanced. He slides a portfolio mix dial from 100/0 to 60/40 and watches his projected sophomore-fall placement probability climb from 31% to 78%, with a real anonymized alum's trajectory animating alongside.
jobs_to_be_done: When I'm deciding which co-ops to apply to, I want to see what actually happens to students who chose like me, so I can make a bet I won't regret in 18 months.
Adjust Your Search Mix in Real Time
success_criteria: Sam, the demo persona, can move from 100/0 to a locked 60/40 commitment in under 6 minutes of interaction, with the headline forecast lift visibly animated.
All cohort renderings enforce k≥15 anonymization; the FERPA disclosure screen is reachable in ≤2 taps from any screen and the underlying NUworks data mapping is fully visible to the user.
At least 2 live AI fetches occur via multi-provider fallback (Claude + Gemini); the Counterfactual Narrative uses Verbalized Sampling with k=3 displayed variants and probabilities.
Primary entities are seeded at 30 / 28 / 26 records respectively, with realistic distributions skewed to reflect the actual diagnostic problem (brand-only majority at week 6).
The prototype visually inhabits Microsoft Teams, Power Automate, Power BI, and SharePoint chrome at appropriate moments; Liz and Jen's names appear verbatim in admin/sender chrome.
Zero verbatim research quotes appear anywhere in the rendered UI; the Theme 5 insight is distilled into product behavior, not displayed as a testimonial.
The Advisor Caseload Dashboard demonstrates cohort-level intervention triage, fulfilling the 'broaden aperture proactively' thesis without a new standalone platform.

hard_constraints.brand: Northeastern University visual marks present but understated; Microsoft Teams / Power BI / Power Automate chrome visible at integration moments.
other: No standalone job board UI — all delivery surfaces are Teams cards or embedded web views launched from Teams
FERPA: k≥15 anonymization on every cohort rendering; anonymization gate visible in the dataflow screen
No verbatim research quotes in product UI; Theme 5 insight distilled into product behavior only
Liz's and Jen's names appear verbatim in stakeholder chrome (sender labels, approval badges)
NUworks remains the system of record; this experience is read-only against it
Tone calibration: encouraging never punitive; no red alarm coloring; celebrations are restrained
